{"content": "1|# make.fun's tiny stack ISA, version 1
2|
3|The instruction set every tiny-stack-vm-01 program is written in. `vm.mjs` beside this file is make.fun's reference
4|VM: the generator runs every drawn program on it, and its output and exit code are the expected answer. Where this
5|page and `vm.mjs` could be read two ways, `vm.mjs` is the rule.
6|
7|## The machine
8|
9|- **Program**: the bytes of `program.bin`, at most 65,535 of them. `pc` starts at 0.
10|- **Values**: 32-bit two's-complement integers. Every arithmetic result wraps modulo 2^32 (so `MUL` is the low 32
11|  bits of the full product, never a rounded floating-point product).
12|- **Data stack**: at most 256 values, empty at the start.
13|- **Call stack**: at most 64 return addresses, empty at the start.
14|- **Memory**: 256 words, addresses 0 to 255, every word 0 at the start.
15|- **Input**: the bytes of `input.bin`, read in order by `IN`.
16|- **Output**: the bytes the program writes (`PRINT`, `PUTC`), at most 65,536 of them.
17|- **Steps**: at most 1,000,000 instructions are executed.
18|
19|## One step
20|
21|In this order:
22|
23|1. If 1,000,000 instructions have already been executed: trap 10.
24|2. If `pc` is outside the program (below 0, or at or past its length): trap 9.
25|3. The byte at `pc` is the opcode; a byte no opcode below names: trap 5.
26|4. If the opcode's immediate does not fit before the end of the program: trap 9.
27|5. The instruction is executed (it counts as one step). Its stack needs are checked first: fewer values than it pops,
28|   trap 2; more than 256 values once it has pushed, trap 3. Then its own traps, then its effect. `pc` moves past the
29|   instruction and its immediate unless the instruction jumps.
30|
31|Immediates are little-endian. In the stack pictures below the rightmost value is the top: `( a b -- r )` pops `b`
32|(the top), then `a`, and pushes `r`.
33|
34|## The opcodes
35|
36|| Byte | Name | Immediate | Stack | Effect |
37||---|---|---|---|---|
38|| 00 | HALT | | | exit with code 0 |
39|| 01 | PUSH8 | 1 byte | `( -- v )` | the byte as a signed 8-bit number, sign-extended (0xFF is -1) |
40|| 02 | PUSH32 | 4 bytes | `( -- v )` | the four bytes as a signed 32-bit number |
41|| 03 | POP | | `( a -- )` | |
42|| 04 | DUP | | `( a -- a a )` | |
43|| 05 | SWAP | | `( a b -- b a )` | |
44|| 06 | OVER | | `( a b -- a b a )` | |
45|| 07 | ROT | | `( a b c -- b c a )` | |
46|| 10 | ADD | | `( a b -- a+b )` | wraps |
47|| 11 | SUB | | `( a b -- a-b )` | wraps |
48|| 12 | MUL | | `( a b -- a*b )` | the low 32 bits of the exact product |
49|| 13 | DIV | | `( a b -- a/b )` | signed, truncated toward zero; b = 0 traps 4; -2147483648 / -1 is -2147483648 |
50|| 14 | MOD | | `( a b -- a%b )` | signed remainder, the sign of `a`; b = 0 traps 4; x % -1 is 0 |
51|| 15 | DIVU | | `( a b -- r )` | a and b read as unsigned 32-bit; the quotient, read back as signed; b = 0 traps 4 |
52|| 16 | MODU | | `( a b -- r )` | the unsigned remainder, read back as signed; b = 0 traps 4 |
53|| 17 | NEG | | `( a -- -a )` | wraps: -(-2147483648) is -2147483648 |
54|| 18 | AND | | `( a b -- a&b )` | bitwise |
55|| 19 | OR | | `( a b -- a\|b )` | bitwise |
56|| 1A | XOR | | `( a b -- a^b )` | bitwise |
57|| 1B | NOT | | `( a -- ~a )` | bitwise complement |
58|| 1C | SHL | | `( a b -- r )` | a shifted left by (b AND 31) bits |
59|| 1D | SHR | | `( a b -- r )` | a shifted right by (b AND 31), arithmetic (the sign bit copied in) |
60|| 1E | SHRU | | `( a b -- r )` | a shifted right by (b AND 31), logical (zeros in), read back as signed |
61|| 20 | EQ | | `( a b -- f )` | 1 if a = b, else 0 |
62|| 21 | LT | | `( a b -- f )` | 1 if a < b as signed numbers, else 0 |
63|| 22 | LTU | | `( a b -- f )` | 1 if a < b as unsigned numbers, else 0 |
64|| 30 | JMP | 2 bytes, signed | | pc = (address of the next instruction) + offset |
65|| 31 | JZ | 2 bytes, signed | `( v -- )` | jump as JMP if v = 0 |
66|| 32 | JNZ | 2 bytes, signed | `( v -- )` | jump as JMP if v is not 0 |
67|| 33 | CALL | 2 bytes, unsigned | | 64 return addresses held already traps 7; else push the next instruction's address and set pc to the immediate |
68|| 34 | RET | | | an empty call stack traps 8; else pc = the popped return address |
69|| 40 | LOAD | | `( addr -- v )` | addr outside 0 to 255 traps 6; else memory[addr] |
70|| 41 | STORE | | `( v addr -- )` | addr outside 0 to 255 traps 6; else memory[addr] = v |
71|| 50 | PRINT | | `( v -- )` | writes v in decimal ASCII: a leading `-` when negative, no other sign, no padding, no newline |
72|| 51 | PUTC | | `( v -- )` | writes one byte, v AND 255 |
73|| 52 | IN | | `( -- b )` | the next input byte, 0 to 255; -1 once the input is used up (and every time after) |
74|| 53 | EXIT | | `( v -- )` | exit with code v AND 255 (so -1 exits 255) |
75|
76|A jump's target is not checked when it jumps: a target outside the program traps 9 at the next step (rule 2). A
77|program that runs past its last byte traps 9 too: falling off the end is never a halt.
78|
79|## Traps
80|
81|A trap ends the program at once. Its exit code is the trap's code; the output it wrote before the trap is kept, and
82|the instruction that trapped writes nothing.
83|
84|| Code | Trap |
85||---|---|
86|| 2 | stack underflow: an instruction pops more values than the stack holds |
87|| 3 | stack overflow: an instruction would leave more than 256 values |
88|| 4 | division by zero: DIV, MOD, DIVU or MODU with b = 0 |
89|| 5 | unknown opcode |
90|| 6 | memory address outside 0 to 255 (LOAD or STORE) |
91|| 7 | call stack overflow: CALL with 64 return addresses held |
92|| 8 | RET with an empty call stack |
93|| 9 | pc outside the program, or an immediate cut off by the program's end |
94|| 10 | step limit: 1,000,000 instructions executed and the program has not ended |
95|| 11 | output limit: a PRINT or PUTC that would take the output past 65,536 bytes (it writes none of its bytes) |
96|
97|## What an entry writes
98|
99|For each program `/input/<id>/program.bin` (with its input `/input/<id>/input.bin`), an entry writes
100|`/output/<id>/stdout.bin`, exactly the bytes the program wrote, and `/output/<id>/exit.txt`, its exit code in
101|decimal (0 to 255; a newline after it is allowed). A program that halts, exits or traps has an exit code; the entry
102|writes it either way.
103|
104|## The rules most implementations get wrong
105|
106|Wrapping 32-bit multiplication; -2147483648 / -1 and -2147483648 % -1; the sign of a remainder; DIVU, MODU and LTU on
107|negative values; shift counts of 32 or more and negative counts (only the low 5 bits count); SHR against SHRU;
